Description

ERK switches on the genes of its own phosphatases, a negative feedback that acts over tens of minutes to hours. The DUSP6 promoter depends on ETS transcription factors, which ERK phosphorylates: ETS1 in lung cancer cells and ETS2 at the conserved ETS site of the promoter [1-3]. ERK phosphorylates the activation domain of ELK1, which then forms a ternary complex with SRF on serum response elements [4, 5], and SRF and ELK1 form such a complex on the DUSP5 promoter and drive its induction by serum [6]. DUSP5 induction needs ERK activity [7]. DUSP5, made in the cytoplasm, enters the nucleus through its own nuclear localisation signal [8]. ERK also limits the cytoplasmic DUSP6: it phosphorylates DUSP6 on Ser159 and Ser197, which does not change its activity but speeds its degradation by the proteasome [9].
